chapter: New York with Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins
title: What shows meant at Cafe Society and accompanying singers like Billie Holiday
summary: Shows were small acts; Thompson disliked accompanying singers as a chore, though Billie Holiday was a pleasure when well, while the piano duo played alone.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: I want to ask you. You said you played back with the shows, am I right,or back of the -- an act or two?

Yes. Well, when I say shows, that can be very deceiving. See a show could mean anything from one group to several groups, and in this particular place it was a very small place and they used to have, as I said, name acts; mainly the show consisted of the band and the piano duo of Pete Johnson, Albert Ammons, and they had a singer. You know, sometimes it would be a singer with her own accompanist, or it would be a singer who would come -- some of them were comedians. I don't remember their names, you know.
Yes.
I never did like to accompany singers myself, you know.
No.
Personally. I did a few things with
Billie Holliday but I was like -- somewhat like Lester in my strict love for jazz.
Yes.

I was always a guy that liked to play jazz. We wanted to play jazz. And we didn't mind playing for singers, really, who we thought were good. Like Billie Holliday was always a pleasure to play with, if she was feeling well, and, you know -- but you know, it just was a thing you did as a chore.
I know, I know.
When you played for someone else, because we wanted to play for ourselves.
I know. The reason really I asked you, in a way,was that because I mean Lester was not a great man for chores, you know --
Right.
-- if he could possibly --
Well, most of -- as I said, was so short.
Yes.

The band had very little to play for the singers, because usually as I said they had their own piano player, or something like that, or like, you know, like Lester maybe didn't play the whole set, you know, like maybe the rhythm section or something like that. It was very short.
Like when I say show -- see, the two piano players, they didn't need anybody, they played alone.
That's right.

You know. Or they played with the drums. If they played the drums, then just the drums. Because they didn't need anybody, they could play -- they made enough rhythm with the two pianos to last a long time.
Yes.
